facts.text: Calibration adjusts a model's parameters to match measurements; validation tests whether the adjusted model predicts unseen measurements. Using the same data for calibration and validation is invalid.
facts.quote: Calibration adjusts a model's parameters until it matches a set of measurements; validation tests whether the adjusted model then predicts measurements it has never seen, and doing both on the same data is cheating.

facts.text: Simulation calibration adjusts parameters such as tire friction on wet gravel, brake-pressure build-up delay and dust attenuation of a laser beam so that a model reproduces a measured test; this calibration is necessary.
facts.quote: Every simulation has knobs: tire friction on wet gravel, the delay before brake pressure builds, how strongly dust weakens a laser beam. Calibration sets the knobs so the model reproduces a measured test, which is necessary.

facts.text: A model can fit its calibration cases perfectly yet fail on the first downhill stop or heavier load because its parameters were tuned to those cases rather than to the physics.
facts.quote: A model can fit its calibration cases perfectly and fail on the first downhill stop or heavier load, because the knobs were tuned to those cases, not to the physics [Chapter 8].

facts.text: Aviation guidance on certifying aircraft seats by analysis states that calibration is not validation.
facts.quote: Aviation guidance on certifying aircraft seats by analysis states that calibration is not validation

facts.text: Aviation guidance on certifying aircraft seats by analysis states that agreement with another validated model is not sufficient to validate a model.
facts.quote: a model cannot be validated merely by agreement with another validated model [Chapter 10].

facts.text: Physical tests should be split in advance into calibration data, validation data and withheld confirmation data.
facts.quote: The practical rule is to split the physical tests in advance into calibration data, validation data and withheld confirmation data

facts.text: The simulation model should be frozen before the validation dataset is used.
facts.quote: freeze the model before touching the validation set [Chapter 10].

facts.text: Within the program's four-month window, there is a temptation to use every expensive prototype stop both to tune the model and to claim validation.
facts.quote: In a four-month window the temptation is to use every expensive prototype stop both to tune the model and to claim validation.

facts.text: An assessor will ask which data calibrated the simulation model and which data remained independent.
facts.quote: An assessor will ask which data calibrated the model and which stayed independent.

facts.text: The booklet recommends never using the same physical stop both to tune a model and to claim validation.
facts.quote: Never use the same stop to both tune and claim validation
